Anya: Quick sync — trying to get apples-to-apples between the replay harness and synthetic generator for streaming vs non-streaming. Replay streaming p99 ~15% higher than synth. Anyone seen this?
Mike: Seen it. My hunch is client read-loop jitter + chunk boundary differences cause backpressure that hits kernel choices.
Sam: Two separate things to check: 1) replay triggers different kernel selection because seq length distribution varies, 2) KV cache warmup/eviction pattern differs between synth and replay.
Iris: Proposal: make a deterministic baseline: fix RNG seeds, normalize seq length histogram, and add a runtime flag to force kernel path for parity (e.g., --kernel-policy=deterministic).
Anya: Can we also capture chunk arrival timestamps at the client boundary? I think a lot of the p99 is explained by jittery chunking rather than model time.
Jordan: I threw together a tiny shim that aligns chunk boundaries to original replay timestamps so we can replay the same arrival pattern against synth. Uploaded to bench infra.
perf-bot: perf-ci: run 2026-03-12T10:23:45Z — results: https://ci.redwood/test-runs/2026-03-12/replay-align-1
Mike: Quick numbers from that run: streaming p99 420ms -> 360ms after aligned-chunking, p50 unchanged. Non-streaming looks stable.
Sam: Also lock batching heuristic for the runs: reduce dynamic batching window from adaptive to a fixed 8ms so long/short sequences aren't mixed. That change reduced variance in a local run.
Iris: Note KV behavior: replay with shuffled conversations caused more cache misses. Run replay with conversation affinity (affinity=conversation_id) to simulate sticky sessions.
Anya: Measurement rules we should follow: warmup of 1000 requests, then collect 1k steady-state requests, run 5 trials, report median of runs and p50/p95/p99; exclude autoscaler transitions and infra noise windows.
Jordan: Also emulate 'slow-drip' client behavior. Our synth generator currently writes the whole request then flushes; production clients stream chunks with small delays which affects server read loop. I added a python read-loop snippet to bench to mimic that.
Jordan: ```python
# simplified client read loop (streamed chunks)
for chunk in chunks:
    sock.send(chunk)
    time.sleep(chunk_interval)  # emulate client drip
# reader side
while not eof:
    data = sock.recv(4096)
    process(data)
```
Sam: Config snippet to fix batching window and kernel policy: ```json
{"batching": {"window_ms": 8, "max_batch": 64}, "runtime": {"kernel_policy": "deterministic", "dump_kernels": true}}
```
Iris: We should capture kernel selection logs (enable --dump-kernels) and correlate p99 points to kernel switch events. Kernel-selection can flip when seq len crosses thresholds.
Anya: Agreed. Next experiments: (a) deterministic-kernel + aligned-chunking replay; (b) same but with conversation-affinity for KV; (c) adaptive-kernel baseline; (d) synth generator with matched chunk pattern. Assign Mike, Sam, Jordan.
Mike: On it — will run (a)+(b) today and post artifacts. :thumbsup:
Sam: One caveat — forcing kernel hides real-world benefits from adaptive selection. We should show both forced (for apples-to-apples) and adaptive (realistic) numbers side-by-side.
Iris: Also add trace ids so we can pull flamegraphs and see if KV reads or kernel GEMM are hot during spikes.
perf-bot: ci-artifact: s3://redwood-perf/benchmarks/replay_vs_synth/1768923456-results.tar.gz
Anya: Perfect. I'll write up a short methodology doc in the bench repo: seed, seq-hist, warmup rules, chunk-alignment steps, flags to capture (--dump-kernels, --disable-adaptive-batching). Then PR.
Jordan: One more note: client read loop backpressure is sensitive to net buffering — run a test with small socket buffers (SO_RCVBUF=32k) to see realistic backpressure.
Mike: Good call. I'll add that knob to the test matrix.
Sam: If we keep seeing p99 gap after all parity controls, we should instrument the runtime for per-request kernel duration and KV miss counters and attach to trace. That will help pinpoint root cause.
Anya: Thanks all — this is actionable. Post results here when ready and we'll fold the methodology into the perf playbook.
